claims.text: Thermomechanical processing can be used to control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Solution annealing, controlled cooling, and aging can tune the volume fraction and distribution of ordered B2 or L12 phases.
Tuning ordered phases can improve mechanical performance by balancing strength and ductility.
The as-cast alloy has a mixed solid-solution matrix with intermetallics distributed non-uniformly.
Solution heat treatment at elevated temperature dissolves precipitates.
Quenching after solution treatment produces a supersaturated solid solution.
Subsequent aging at intermediate temperatures precipitates ordered phases.
A suitable treatment is solution annealing at approximately 1100–1200 °C for 1–2 hours, water or oil quenching, and aging at 600–800 °C for 2–12 hours.
B2 and L12 phases can nucleate and grow within FCC or BCC matrices in this alloy system.
The nucleation and growth kinetics of ordered phases are influenced by thermal history and solute diffusivity.
The proposed processing steps create non-equilibrium conditions and strategic diffusion pathways.
These non-equilibrium conditions and diffusion pathways permit controlled precipitation of strengthening phases.
The processing limits unwanted coarsening or segregation and thereby refines the overall microstructure.
The treatment will increase the amount and uniformity of B2 or L12 intermetallic phases.
The treated alloy will have higher yield strength without a severe loss of ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
The as-cast baseline contains coarser or inhomogeneously distributed intermetallics.
The as-cast baseline has relatively lower mechanical stability under loading.
Excessively high treatment temperatures or prolonged soak times can coarsen the particles.
Particle coarsening diminishes the strength benefit.
The optimal treatment temperatures and times depend on the alloy composition and initial microstructure.

contradictions.description: The method is labeled thermomechanical processing, but the specified intervention contains only thermal treatments and no mechanical deformation step.
